_meta.active: BISMUTH SUBCITRATE POTASSIUM; METRONIDAZOLE; TETRACYCLINE HYDROCHLORIDE
_meta.indication: PYLERA capsules, in combination with omeprazole, are indicated for the treatment of patients with Helicobacter pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (active or history of within the past 5 years) to eradicate H. pylori
_meta.receipt_date: October 2, 2001 (original NDA received); resubmission/complete response received March 27, 2006

pivotal_trials.trial_name: HPST99-CUS01 (North American pivotal Phase III trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, parallel group, open-label (investigator blinded), active-controlled study comparing 10-day Helicide capsules plus omeprazole (OBMT) versus omeprazole, amoxicillin, and clarithromycin (OAC)
pivotal_trials.population: Helicobacter pylori positive patients with current duodenal ulcer or a history of duodenal ulcer disease, in the United States and Canada
pivotal_trials.endpoint: H. pylori eradication rate, defined as two negative 13C-urea breath tests performed at 4 and 8 weeks post-therapy
pivotal_trials.n: 299 patients received study therapy (147 OBMT and 152 OAC)
pivotal_trials.result: Per-Protocol eradication: OBMT 92.5% [87.8, 97.2] (n=120) vs OAC 85.7% [76.9, 91.8] (n=126), difference 6.8 [-0.9, 14.5]; Modified Intent-to-Treat: OBMT 87.7% [82.2, 93.2] (n=138) vs OAC 83.2% [77.0, 89.5] (n=137), difference 4.5 [-3.9, 12.8] — demonstrating non-inferiority (lower bounds of -3.9% MITT and -0.9% PP are above the non-inferiority margin of -15%)

key_safety: Most common adverse events in the OBMT arm (incidence >1%) were stool abnormality 15.6%, diarrhea 8.8%, dyspepsia 8.8%, abdominal pain 8.8%, nausea 8.2%, and headache 8.2%; gastrointestinal AEs were the most commonly reported
target_moa: Fixed combination of three antimicrobial agents (bismuth subcitrate potassium, metronidazole, tetracycline hydrochloride) given with the proton pump inhibitor omeprazole; triple antimicrobial therapy with a PPI eradicates H. pylori
modality: small molecule (fixed-combination of three small-molecule/metal-salt antimicrobials)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: Metronidazole has been shown to be carcinogenic in mice and rats; unnecessary use of the drug should be avoided and its use reserved for the conditions described in Indications and Usage

summary.text: PYLERA was approved under section 505(b)(2) of the FD&C Act, relying on FDA's previous findings of safety and effectiveness for Helidac (NDA 50-719) and published literature, supported by one pivotal North American Phase III trial (HPST99-CUS01); approval followed two prior not approvable letters for chemistry deficiencies.

citations.quote: Under Section 505(b)(2) of the FD&C Act, the applicant referenced the FDA's findings of safety and effectiveness from NDA 50-719 (Helidac® therapy containing bismuth subsalicylate, metronidazole, and tetracycline for the eradication of *H. pylori*), and literature articles on the efficacy of the combination of omeprazole, bismuth, metronidazole, and tetracycline (OBMT) therapy.
The applicant conducted one pivotal Phase III trial in North America (HPST99-CUS01) to document the efficacy of Helicide therapy plus omeprazole.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of patients with H. pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (active or history of within the past 5 years) to eradicate H. pylori in pediatric patients ages >2 to 16 when used in combination with omeprazole; final report submission September 30, 2011
